gpus.prompt: Batch-1 decoding of a 7B model in bf16 on a GPU with 3 TB/s of memory bandwidth: what is the best-case tokens per second? (nearest 10)
gpus.explanation: Each token reads all 14 GB of weights: 3000 GB/s ÷ 14 GB ≈ 214 tokens/s at most.

gpus.prompt: Which operations are typically memory-bound? (select all)
gpus.explanation: Large matmuls do many FLOPs per byte and are compute-bound.
FlashAttention and torch.compile both rely on fusion.
options: It reduces memory traffic by doing several operations on data while it is on-chip
It reduces the number of parameters

gpus.explanation: Good large-scale training runs reach roughly 40–60%.
options: Achieved useful model FLOP/s divided by the hardware's peak FLOP/s

distributed.prompt: In data parallelism, what is communicated between GPUs every step?
distributed.explanation: Each GPU holds a full model copy and processes a different slice of the batch.

distributed.prompt: Which ZeRO stage also shards the model weights themselves (equivalent to FSDP)?
distributed.explanation: Stage 1 shards optimizer states, stage 2 adds gradients, stage 3 adds weights.

distributed.prompt: A pipeline has 4 stages and 12 micro-batches. What fraction of time is the bubble, (p−1)/(m+p−1)(p-1)/(m+p-1)(p−1)/(m+p−1)? (three decimals)
distributed.explanation: 3/15=0.23/15=0.23/15=0.2. More micro-batches shrink the bubble.

distributed.prompt: Why is tensor parallelism usually kept within a single node?
distributed.explanation: NVLink-class bandwidth inside a node makes per-layer collectives affordable.
options: It needs very fast links because activations are exchanged every layer

ml-system-design.prompt: What should come first in an ML system design answer?
ml-system-design.explanation: The design depends on latency, scale and what success means.
options: Clarifying the goal, users, scale and constraints

ml-system-design.prompt: 100 million daily users make 20 requests each. Roughly what is the average QPS? (nearest thousand)
ml-system-design.explanation: 2×109/86,400≈23,0002\times10^9/86{,}400\approx23{,}0002×109/86,400≈23,000 requests per second; plan for peaks of 2–3×.

ml-system-design.prompt: Which signals indicate seniority in a design interview? (select all)
ml-system-design.explanation: Interviewers listen for judgement, not buzzwords.
options: Starting with a simple baseline before a complex model
Explicit trade-offs between latency, quality and cost
A plan for monitoring and iteration after launch

case-studies.prompt: For payment fraud detection, why choose the threshold by expected cost?
case-studies.explanation: Expected cost (and review capacity) define the right operating point.
options: Missed fraud and blocked good customers have very different costs

case-studies.prompt: In feed recommendation, why optimize for long-term satisfaction rather than clicks alone?
case-studies.explanation: Multi-objective ranking balances engagement with quality signals.
options: Click optimization rewards clickbait and can hurt retention

case-studies.prompt: In content moderation, recall targets should be higher for the most severe harm categories.
case-studies.explanation: Missing severe content is far costlier than extra review for less severe categories.

__exam.prompt: Inference for a 13B model is too slow at batch size 1. Which changes raise throughput the most? (select all)
__exam.explanation: Decoding is memory-bound; batching and fewer bytes per weight help directly.

__exam.prompt: A 7B model needs about 112 GB for training state with Adam. With ZeRO-3 across 8 GPUs, roughly how many GB per GPU (before activations)?
__exam.explanation: 112 / 8 = 14 GB when weights, gradients and optimizer states are all sharded.

__exam.prompt: What is the arithmetic intensity of adding two fp16 vectors (1 FLOP per element, 6 bytes moved)? (two decimals)
In a recommendation system design, where should the heavy model with rich cross features run?
__exam.explanation: Candidate generation narrows the set first.
options: In the ranking stage, on a few hundred candidates
On every item in the catalogue
